label: Xl Recordings
release_notes: Fifth album from the Dublin band, after Romance (2024). Produced by James Ford, who took over from Dan Carey (producer of the first three albums) on Romance.

Ford is also a member of Simian Mobile Disco and The Last Shadow Puppets, and has produced Arctic Monkeys and Depeche Mode (Memento Mori). Marta Salogni engineered; she also recorded and mixed Memento Mori and has worked with Björk and Bon Iver. Matt Colton mastered.
Recorded mostly at Decoy Studios in Suffolk, plus Narcissus Studios in London. Grian Chatten cut his vocals separately with Ford in Palermo, Sicily.

Grian Chatten - vocals, guitar; Carlos O'Connell - guitar, synths; Conor Curley - guitar; Conor Deegan - bass; Tom Coll - drums. Rosalía guests on Where Is Gone?, the band's first guest vocalist. Strings arranged by Chatten, Richard Jones, Laura Moody and Elysian Collective.
About the doomscroll and phone-as-painkiller culture, technological dependence and collapse. Chatten says he left the hope out on purpose (Rolling Stone Philippines).

pull_quotes.text: gloomy, gorgeous and a gargantuan triumph
a dark but exhilarating reflection of end times
This is cruel, beautiful feel-bad music.

draft_comment: Dublin post-punk gone synth-heavy and string-laced, again with James Ford and a Rosalía duet. Critics hear Depeche Mode, The Cure and New Order. Tongue and Japan are FCC.

tracks.title: Six Shot Morning
tracks.notes: Synth intro, then a heavy bassline and a cool, commanding male lead vocal (Rolling Stone Philippines). Mechanical Depeche Mode death march (NME); gated, grainy drums (The Soundboard).

tracks.title: Marianne
tracks.notes: Ballad with gauzy synths and spiralling strings (The Soundboard, Guardian). Cyborg-meets-symphony balladry (NME); Moroder-style electronic tone with a Duran Duran feel (Beats Per Minute).

tracks.title: Mimesis
tracks.notes: Dominant bass, sharp snare hits and cold synths (Beats Per Minute). New Order-style bassline (Guardian); 80s dance-pop feel (Rolling Stone Philippines).

tracks.title: Happy For You
tracks.notes: Flanged, Cure-like guitar twang (Guardian, Rolling Stone Philippines), building to a massive guitar drop (AllMusic, The Soundboard). Bitter, sarcastic song about a breakup (Beats Per Minute).

tracks.title: Demolition
tracks.notes: Sweeping open guitars and crunching synths into a big chorus (The Soundboard). Drum machine pulse (Rolling Stone Philippines); grunge attack (Guardian); Smiths-like guitar lead (Beats Per Minute).

tracks.title: Tongue
tracks.notes: Tempo check: songbpm says ~165 BPM, but critics hear trip-hop beats, so it may be half-time. Slinky bassline and piano (Rolling Stone Philippines); hollowed, heavy mix with a piano interlude (The Soundboard) and a jazzy bridge (Beats Per Minute). Trip-hop gloom (NME). Listed in FCC Edit Needed.

tracks.title: One Man
tracks.notes: Tempo check: songbpm says ~132 BPM, but critics call it a ballad, so it may be half-time. Epic, string-drenched romantic ballad that builds to a big finish (Beats Per Minute). Breathy and elegiac (NME).

tracks.title: Where Is Gone? (with ROSALÍA)
tracks.notes: Features Rosalía: male and female vocals together on an orchestral duet. Restrained strings, alt-country feel (The Soundboard); Morricone-style ballad (NME, Guardian). No FCC words in the English lyrics posted; Spanish checked for common swear words.

tracks.title: You Miss Me
tracks.notes: Smoky guitar hook (Rolling Stone Philippines). Edgy synth strings and sharp beats in the verses, string-led crooner chorus (Beats Per Minute); Robert Smith-style verse (NME).

tracks.title: Japan
tracks.notes: Bittersweet acoustic singalong (NME). Dream-pop feel, Beach House meets a-ha (Beats Per Minute).

tracks.title: Intimate
tracks.notes: Skittering sci-fi hymn (NME). Hi-hat-driven headbanger of a closer (Rolling Stone Philippines).

sources: Lyrics screened on Genius (counts only): all 11 tracks. FCC words on tracks 6 and 10.
